name: Valeri Liukin
milestone_by_age_26: Won four gold medals at the 1987 European Championships in Moscow (all-around, horizontal bar, floor exercise, parallel bars) and team gold at the 1987 World Championships, all at age 20.
early_history_summary: Liukin began gymnastics at age 7 in Aktyubinsk, Kazakhstan, and moved to Moscow to join the Soviet Junior National team, making his international debut at the 1983 Friendship Cup at age 16. He made the Soviet national team in 1985 at age 18 and rapidly became one of the world's top gymnasts, winning four European Championship golds in 1987.
family_context_summary: Born in Aktyubinsk, Kazakh SSR, Soviet Union; family background beyond his gymnastics training is not documented in reviewed sources. He married 1987 World Champion rhythmic gymnast Anna Kotchneva while still competing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet national team pipeline, early specialization, gymnastics academy
evidence_summary: Liukin started gymnastics at age 7 and was moved to Moscow to join the Soviet Junior National team, making his international debut at 16. The Soviet gymnastics system provided elite coaching, facilities, and competitive exposure from a young age. By 20, he won four golds at the European Championships and was the first gymnast to perform a triple back somersault on floor. No family background details are documented beyond his birth in Kazakhstan and later move to Moscow for training.
starting_point: Born in Aktyubinsk, Kazakh SSR, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Gymnastics coach and co-founder of WOGA in Plano, Texas; former Soviet Olympic champion; inducted into International Gymnastics Hall of Fame in 2005.

name: Gérson
milestone_by_age_26: Made professional debut for Flamengo in 1959 at age 18 and was immediately selected for the Brazilian team at the Pan-American Games; by age 20 he was in Brazil's full national squad and a starting playmaker for Flamengo.
early_history_summary: Gérson grew up in Niterói, Brazil, in a footballing family — his father and uncle were both professional footballers in Rio. He joined Flamengo's youth setup and made his professional debut in 1959, rapidly becoming the team's playmaker and being compared to the legendary Didi. Within a year he was selected for the Pan-American Games, and by 1961 he was in Brazil's full national squad.
family_context_summary: Born in Niterói, Brazil; both his father and uncle were professional footballers in Rio. His father was a close friend of Zizinho, widely held as the best Brazilian footballer before Pelé. The family had deep connections in Rio's football world.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father and uncle were professional footballers in Rio; father was close friends with Zizinho, a Brazilian football legend, giving Gérson direct exposure to elite football culture from childhood.

evidence_summary: Gérson was born into a footballing family in Niterói — his father and uncle were both professional players, and his father's close friendship with Zizinho gave him unusual access to Brazil's elite football world. He joined Flamengo and made his professional debut at 18, was selected for the Pan-American Games within a year, and was in Brazil's full national squad by 20. The Rio football ecosystem of the late 1950s, with clubs like Flamengo and Botafogo, was one of the world's most competitive environments, providing direct domain immersion from childhood.

name: Armi Kuusela
milestone_by_age_26: Won the inaugural Miss Universe pageant on June 28, 1952 at age 17, becoming the first-ever Miss Universe and a global cultural icon.
early_history_summary: Kuusela was one of six children born to Finnish parents who owned a small family business in Muhos, Finland. She was unexpectedly invited to participate in Finland's national beauty pageant after her boarding school roommate's mother responded to a public notice. She won Suomen Neito (Miss Finland) on May 24, 1952, which qualified her to represent Finland at the first Miss Universe pageant in Long Beach, California, where she won at age 17.
family_context_summary: Born in Muhos, Finland, one of six children; parents owned and operated a small family business; her father was a decorated veteran who fought for Finland during World War II.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having domain-relevant expertise; family ran a small business.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Miss Universe inaugural pageant, global media platform, Finnish national selection
evidence_summary: Kuusela was a 17-year-old from a small family business background in Muhos, Finland, when she was unexpectedly invited to compete in the national beauty pageant. She won Miss Finland and then the inaugural Miss Universe competition in 1952, becoming a global cultural icon. The Miss Universe platform itself was the structural wave — the inaugural pageant created instant worldwide fame. No evidence of family domain advantage, coaching, or early training in pageantry; her win appears to have been driven by natural appearance and the novelty of the competition.

He was the youngest member of the legendary Italian épée team that won Olympic gold at the 1960 Rome Games. His international breakthrough came even earlier — at 18, he was part of Italy's World Championship gold medal team in Paris in 1957. He continued winning at the highest level through the 1960s.

name: Mate Parlov
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Yugoslav national amateur boxing title in 1967 at age 18, beginning a run of eight consecutive national titles; by age 26 he had also won two European Championship golds (1971, 1973) and the inaugural World Amateur Championship gold (1974).
early_history_summary: Parlov was born in Split, Yugoslavia (now Croatia), the youngest of four children. His family moved to Pula when he was 10. He started training at the boxing school in Pula, which opened in December 1964 when he was 16, under coaches Aldo Banovac and Aldo Buršić. BK Pula was his only club. He won his first Yugoslav national title at 18 in 1967 and rapidly rose to become European and World amateur champion.
